nodes.rationale: Written as a study companion to the project README, which remains the single source of truth for current file layout and known limitations.

nodes.label: OnPaper README
nodes.rationale: Declared the single source of truth: documents the real current layout; the older app/ + core/ proposal in past docs was never implemented.

nodes.label: requirements.txt
nodes.rationale: Lists direct dependencies only; pip resolves everything else (pandas, pyarrow, scipy) to versions that ship prebuilt wheels for whatever Python the host runs, so a deploy never falls back to compiling numpy/scipy from source.

nodes.label: Machine Learning Applications in Healthcare: A Comprehensive Review
nodes.norm_label: machine learning applications in healthcare: a comprehensive review

nodes.label: Always return useful partial results
nodes.rationale: RAG returns the retrieved passages even when the LLM answer fails, so the feature stays useful offline.

nodes.label: Batch, don't loop
nodes.rationale: Vectorize everything at once and do a single matrix op. The earlier plagiarism check ran an O(input x reference) loop of individual transform() calls and took 10s+; one batched transform plus one cosine matrix runs in under 1s. Called the single most important performance lesson in the repo.

nodes.label: Graceful degradation
nodes.rationale: Core philosophy: every external dependency degrades gracefully and never crashes the app. Almost every module has a try/except that swaps a powerful path for a simpler one (no AI key, no torch/transformers, no Gemini SDK, no NLTK punkt).

nodes.label: Guarded imports
nodes.rationale: Heavy or optional libraries (google-genai, torch, transformers) are imported inside try/except so a missing package disables one feature instead of crashing the app.

nodes.label: L2 normalization
nodes.rationale: Vectors are scaled to length 1 so that a plain dot product equals cosine similarity.

nodes.label: Lazy + once loading
nodes.rationale: Models load lazily on first use (embedder _load()) or once at import as a module global (plagiarism_detector); Streamlit's re-run model makes this essential.

nodes.label: Lexical-only fallback
nodes.rationale: When transformers/torch embeddings are unavailable, RAG chat falls back from semantic+lexical to TF-IDF-only retrieval and still answers.

nodes.label: NLTK punkt fallback
nodes.rationale: If the NLTK punkt model is missing, sentence tokenization falls back to a naive text.split('.').

nodes.label: Single AI gateway
nodes.rationale: One gateway for all AI: every feature that needs an LLM calls generate_text(prompt), which routes to Groq then Ollama (then Gemini); features never talk to an LLM API directly.

nodes.label: Streamlit re-run model
nodes.rationale: Streamlit re-runs the script from the top on every widget interaction, which is why heavy objects are loaded as module-level globals so a .pkl loads once at import, not on every click.

nodes.label: Three-layer architecture
nodes.rationale: The UI knows nothing about TF-IDF or HTTP, the services know nothing about Streamlit, and models are just artifacts loaded by services; this separation is what lets each piece fail independently.

nodes.label: AI Backends (auto mode: Groq then Ollama)
nodes.norm_label: ai backends (auto mode: groq then ollama)
nodes.rationale: Open-source models only; auto mode tries fast cloud Groq first, then local Ollama, and surfaces the real backend error (e.g. Groq 401/429) instead of a generic not-available message.

nodes.label: pypdf over PyPDF2
nodes.rationale: PDFs are parsed with the maintained pypdf because its predecessor PyPDF2 is unmaintained and has a known vulnerability (PYSEC-2026-1835).

nodes.label: Optional torch + transformers (intentionally not listed)
nodes.rationale: torch and transformers are heavy (large download, can exceed free-tier memory) and only power two optional features (perplexity-based AI detector, dense-embedding chat retrieval), both of which import them lazily and fall back gracefully when absent. Enable locally with pip install torch>=2.6 transformers>=4.44,<6.

nodes.label: Gemini
nodes.rationale: README is internally inconsistent: the intro and the Grammar Check row still name Gemini, while the AI Backends section says Gemini has been removed and the gemini_helper filename is kept only for import compatibility.

nodes.label: Regex fallback
nodes.rationale: If the AI API is unavailable or returns no JSON, grammar check still applies common contraction, spelling and punctuation fixes.

nodes.label: Hybrid RAG
nodes.rationale: Sentence-aware chunks (~130 words, 1-sentence overlap) are indexed lexically (TF-IDF, always available) and semantically (MiniLM, optional); both rankings are fused with RRF (k=60), a grounded prompt plus the last 3 conversation turns goes to generate_text(), and retrieved passages are always returned.

nodes.label: Noisy-OR
nodes.rationale: Probabilistic way to fuse several independent 'yes' signals (perplexity model, HC3 classifier, style heuristics) into one AI-likelihood probability.

nodes.label: RRF (Reciprocal Rank Fusion)
nodes.rationale: Combines two ranked lists by summing 1/(k+rank) with k=60; chosen because it is scale-free and robust, so TF-IDF and embedding scores need no calibration against each other.

nodes.label: Prompt-injection guard
nodes.rationale: Reviewer and chat prompts mark the uploaded document as material to analyse, not instructions; this lowers the risk of text in a paper steering the AI but cannot remove it.

nodes.label: CI workflow (.github/workflows/ci.yml)
nodes.rationale: Besides running tests on every push, it opens the live app in a headless browser every 6 hours because Streamlit sleeps apps after about 12 hours without visitors.

nodes.label: pip-audit
nodes.rationale: CI runs pip-audit on every push and every Monday and fails on any known vulnerability; the workflow token is read-only.

nodes.label: Caching invalidated on change
nodes.rationale: Reference sentences are tokenized once and cached in _ref_sentences_cache, which is cleared whenever the reference set changes.

nodes.label: Surface the real error
nodes.rationale: auto mode reports the actual backend failure (API_KEY_INVALID, Groq 429) instead of a generic message, via is_unavailable_response() and last_error tracking.

nodes.label: Analysis cache cap
nodes.rationale: Caches of analysed text are capped at 50 entries and expire after an hour so visitors' text does not linger in server memory.

nodes.label: Error sanitisation
nodes.rationale: Avoids leaking internals to visitors: no Python tracebacks (client.showErrorDetails = none), provider organisation IDs and key-like strings stripped from AI error messages, generic file-read errors.

nodes.label: Input size limits
nodes.rationale: Stops one huge upload or paste exhausting memory or CPU: text cut to 200,000 characters, PDFs to 300 pages, pairwise comparison to 2,000 sentences, browser messages to 10 MB. On an 877,000-character input the repetition finder went from 187 s and 1 GB to 3 s and 71 MB.

nodes.label: MAX_PROMPT_CHARS
nodes.rationale: The AI gateway refuses any prompt over 60,000 characters before sending it, so one visitor cannot burn the shared AI quota.

nodes.label: Security
nodes.rationale: OnPaper is public and takes untrusted files and text, so every input is bounded and nothing internal is shown to visitors. Not covered: no per-visitor rate limit, and the pickled models in src/ML/ are trusted because they ship with the repo.
